header.name: Computer Aided Drug Design
header.description: This course teaches the principles and practice of dug discovery, molecular mechanics and biomolecular simulations with an emphasis on the practical skills needed to perform and interpret simulations of biological macromolecules. In addition, this course will also introduce Molecular Docking technique that is essential for Computational Drug Design.
prerequisites_desirable: Basic knowledge of biology, chemistry, physics and python
prerequisites_desirable_resolved: Basic knowledge of biology, chemistry, physics and python

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students can describe the relation of protein evolution with its function and explain fundamental structural properties

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students can develop models of biomolecules utilizing the principles of molecular mechanics and execute small simulations of biomolecules

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students can compute meaningful Thermodynamic and Kinetic analysis from simulation trajectory and are able to correlate the underlying connection with statistical physics.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students can design the basic computational drug design experiments and are able to construct projects using molecular docking and simulation techniques.

lecture_topics: Structure-Function relation and properties of protein
Concept of molecular Force Fields and Thermostats.
Understanding the dynamics - Introduction of of simulation Molecular Dynamics
Extracting Thermodynamics and Kinetics data from simulation trajectory
understanding the concept of equilibrium in simulation
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Assignment:  (1) where students will actually simulate protein/DNA or their interactions using computers.
Assignment:  (2) where students will actually simulate protein using computers.

lecture_topics: Analyzing the trajectories to understand biophysical parameters
Theoretical basis of Molecular Docking and hands on experience with AUTODOCK
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Projects will be given to understand the basics of computational drug designing and how to use molecular docking tools. Students will study the interactions of proteins and protein-small drug molecules using AUTODOCK.

resources.title: Molecular modelling: Principles and Applications by Andrew R. Leach
Computational Drug Design by David C Young
Voit E (2012) A First Course in Systems Biology. Garland Science, 1/e. ISBN 0815344678
